source.title: Mid-Ulster Mail, 26 April 1930, p. 8 ("Cookstown Rural Council nominations: no contest")
source.publisher: Mid-Ulster Mail (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: returned unopposed: the only nomination for the division in 'a complete list of the nominations lodged' with the returning officer, Mr. Wm. Jas. Glasgow (Mid-Ulster Mail, 26 April 1930, p. 8, page image read); Munterevlin was the only division polled

note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors, polled on Wednesday 4 June 1930 and counted at the council boardroom on the morning of 5 June (queue nominal 29 May). Munterevlin was the only contest in the district; the other divisions were returned unopposed and their names are not printed in the reports traced. Filed on 1930-06-04, the polling day for county council and rural district elections in Co. Tyrone that year (confirmed); previously filed under 1930-06-05 (verification 5 Nov 2026). The five new members returned unopposed are added from the Ulster Herald of 26 April 1930, p. 5; the re-nominated outgoing members are not named there (6 Nov 2026). The ten other divisions are added from the Mid-Ulster Mail's complete list of the nominations (26 April 1930, p. 8), which prints one nomination for each division except Munterevlin, where it marks Mr. Patrick J. Quinn's nomination 'invalid'; Munterevlin was nevertheless polled (7 Nov 2026). Returned unopposed.
